(i) a new method for analyzing functional MRI time series is proposed, and (ii) the new method is shown to be valid in the presence and absence of intrinsic autocorrelation.

(a) a new method for analyzing functional MRI data has been developed that can detect significant correlations between sensory input, as modeled in the time domain, and the hemodynamic brain response; (b) this new method has been implemented and tested on simulated data; and (c) this new method is being implemented and tested on experimental data from a visual motion task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of functional magnetic resonance imaging data.
the study of the brain's response to sensory input,
the development of a method for detecting significant correlations between the sensory input and the physiological response of the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method presented in this paper is a valid method of detecting significant and regionalspecific correlations between sensory input (stimulus) and the hemodynamic (physiological) response.

, in the present work we have shown that, the use of the cross-correlation function is a valid approach to detecting significant and region-specific correlations between sensory input (or other input) and the hemodynamic responses.

, in the absence of an adequate model, there is no way to determine the true nature of the hemodynamic impulse response, and therefore, there is no valid method for determining the true nature of a hemodynamic response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hemodynamic response to a stimulus is not a simple linear function of the stimulus, but is a function which depends on the stimulus and the brain's response to the stimulus.

we have presented a method for detecting significant correlations between sensory input, such as visual or somatosensory stimulation, and the hemodynamic responses in the brain, as measured with MRI, and that we have demonstrated the validity of this approach.
we have developed a new method of analyzing functional MRI time series that is based on the use of cross-correlation functions between sensory input and brain activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is not just a passive recipient of sensory information.
the hemodynamic response is not just a function of the input, but also a function of the brain state, and this can be seen in the data.
the brain is not a static entity. Rather it is a highly dynamic, ever changing system.
